# a11y.aria-attributes — ARIA attribute does not exist or has an invalid value

- **Check ID:** `a11y.aria-attributes`
- **Default severity:** `error`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** WCAG 4.1.2
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/a11y.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/a11y.aria-attributes.md`](../a11y.aria-attributes.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

An `aria-*` attribute is not a WAI-ARIA attribute, or its value is not one the attribute accepts.

## Why it matters

Assistive technology ignores `aria-*` attributes it does not know, and it ignores values it cannot read. `aria-lable="Search"` gives the button no name; `aria-expanded="yes"` tells a screen reader nothing about whether a menu is open. Both fail silently and look fine on screen, so they usually survive until someone tests with a screen reader.

## What it checks

- **Unknown name** (error): any attribute starting with `aria-` that is not in WAI-ARIA 1.2. If a real name is within two edits, the report says "Did you mean" and offers an exact rename.
- **Invalid value** (error), by the type each attribute takes:
  - true or false: `aria-atomic`, `aria-busy`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-modal`, `aria-multiline`, `aria-multiselectable`, `aria-readonly`, `aria-required`
  - true, false, or undefined: `aria-expanded`, `aria-hidden`, `aria-selected`, `aria-grabbed`
  - true, false, mixed, or undefined: `aria-checked`, `aria-pressed`
  - one fixed token: `aria-autocomplete`, `aria-current`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-live`, `aria-orientation`, `aria-sort`
  - a list of fixed tokens: `aria-relevant`, `aria-dropeffect`
  - a whole number: `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-colcount`, `aria-colindex`, `aria-colspan`, `aria-rowcount`, `aria-rowindex`, `aria-rowspan`, each with its minimum
  - a number: `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`

Text and id-reference attributes (`aria-label`, `aria-description`, `aria-labelledby`, and so on) accept any value here; ids are checked by [`a11y.aria-references`](a11y.aria-references.md). Attribute names are not case sensitive in HTML; tokens must be written in lowercase.

## How to fix

```html
<!-- before -->
<button aria-lable="Search">🔍</button>
<button aria-expanded="yes">Menu</button>

<!-- after -->
<button aria-label="Search">🔍</button>
<button aria-expanded="true">Menu</button>
```

The report gives an exact edit for a misspelled name and for a value that differs from a valid one only by letter case (`True` to `true`). For other values it names the allowed ones, because a word like `yes` could mean either.

## Options

None.

## Standards

- [WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html)
- [WAI-ARIA 1.2: states and properties](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#state_prop_def)
